=== HANDOFF #4 — epic e369 (Jira Server/Data Center). READ FIRST. ===

BOARD (verified, not remembered)
  e369 epic        in_progress
  8c35 J8  story   IN_PROGRESS, claimed. ADR 0055 MERGED (change 1107). Ready to CLOSE.
  bda8 J9  story   IN_PROGRESS, claimed. All code MERGED (1105/1106/1108). Live-verified. Ready to CLOSE.
  bb8c J10 story   CLOSED certified.
  5200 J11 story   OPEN. Plan at review round 4 (rounds 1-3 blocked; all findings now fixed).
  b586     story   OPEN. Rate limiter, now IN SCOPE by operator direction.
  21fc 387d 7c26 9263 f391  bugs OPEN — see 'defect-free' below.
  a357     bug     OPEN — implemented BY bda8; close when bda8 closes.
  6a91 cc77 dbf9 06e0 — open, deliberately OUT of this epic.

WORKTREE /Users/joeoakhart/rebar-jira-family @ 8ffdcea0d, clean. ALWAYS: export PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH"

THE STANDARD THE OPERATOR SET: 'the implicit acceptance criteria is shipping defect free code.' That
is why 387d and 7c26 are IN scope despite being pre-existing and not DC-specific — shipping DC support
ships those paths to a new deployment type. My earlier 'pre-existing therefore follow-up' framing was
retired; the live Cloud bridge escapes both only because its trigger conditions (permanent
identity-write failure; project moves) do not occur there, not because Cloud is immune.

WHAT IS PROVEN, AND WHAT IS NOT
 * PROVEN LIVE: a DC writing pass converges cleanly — 'OK: steady-state pass converged' on a real
   instance, no traceback (CI run 30637886718).
 * NOT PROVEN: that data MOVES. That run reported scanned=0 — it converged because the store was
   EMPTY. The epic's headline operator-attested AC (an issue created in DC appears locally; a local
   edit appears in DC) has NO evidence. J11 exists to get it. Do not close the epic on 'converged'.

REMAINING TO CLOSE THE EPIC: close 8c35 and bda8 (both ready); land J11 (live proof); b586; and the
four shipped-code defects 21fc, 387d, 7c26, 9263 — plus f391 FIRST, because J11 runs on a harness that
currently dies at setup on the 10-PAT cap.

HARD-WON, EXPENSIVE LESSONS — these cost real time, please carry them
 1. COUNTS ARE NOT CAUSES. All three live runs reported '2 failed, 12 passed, 1 error' with three
    DIFFERENT causes. Read the error text every time.
 2. ABSENCE OF ERRORS IS NOT EVIDENCE OF FUNCTION. 7 of the 12 transport members were swallowed by
    'except Exception' at every call site; 'nothing raised' was true while nothing worked.
 3. WHEN A PLAN KEEPS RETURNING DOUBLE-DIGIT FINDINGS, SUSPECT STRUCTURE. J9 blocked 8 times; splitting
    the exception contract into J10 produced a first-try PASS.
 4. AFTER EDITING A PLAN, GREP THE WHOLE DOCUMENT FOR THE TERM YOU CHANGED. Six BLOCK rounds came from
    revising the analysis and leaving Scope or the ACs stale. Once I introduced a contradiction while
    fixing the very thing it contradicted.
 5. ON FINDING A DEFECT CLASS, SWEEP FOR SIBLINGS. I fixed pagination in get_parent_map and left the
    same bug in get_issuelinks_map and get_comment_map (9263).
 6. VERIFY MECHANISMS, NOT PLAUSIBILITY. I twice asserted a mechanism I had not traced — 'prev_snapshot
    drives mass deletion' (it is a baseline store for bound tickets) and 'the local harness fails on
    resource contention' (the README documents arm64 emulation; the image is linux/amd64 only).
 7. LIVE TESTING IS THE ORACLE — AND STILL NOT SUFFICIENT. The harness is ONE default-configured
    8.17.1 instance: no index lag, no lowered page cap, no rate limiting, no restricted screens. Every
    OSS-comparison finding was invisible to it.
 8. pycontribs/jira is the AUTHORITATIVE interface; its API is SPLIT across jira.JIRA and
    jira.resources.Issue, and @translate_resource_args defeats STATIC lookup — verify at runtime.

MECHANICS: plan-review certified BEFORE claim; review-plan FAST-FAILS on a blocked ticket; editing a
plan stales its attestation; SERIALIZE LLM gates (one review or one close at a time); Gerrit needs
LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1 then POST /a/changes/<n>/submit -d '{}'; Gerrit REBASES on submit so
verify landed CONTENT then 'git reset --hard origin/main'; commits need 50-char subject / 72-col body,
a rebar-ticket trailer, -s, and the venv on PATH.
